title: Acceptance characterizes the verifier language
statement: Let $c$ be a machine representation scheme and $z$ a bit string. The result produced from $z$ by the guarded computation equals the two-bit word $11$ if and only if $z$ belongs to the verifier language: the set of words $y'w'$ such that $|w'|=|y'|+1$ and there exist bit strings $\beta,v$ and natural numbers $n',t'$ with $y'=\langle\beta,\langle v,\langle1^{n'},1^{t'}\rangle\rangle\rangle$, for which the machine decoded from $\beta$ halts within $t'$ steps on input $\langle v,w'_{[:n'] }\rangle$ with output exactly $1$.
replaced: Let $c$ be a machine-representation scheme, which assigns to every bit string $\alpha$ a one-work-tape binary Turing machine $M_\alpha$ (decoding is total). For a bit string $z$, write $s(z)$ for its odd split (the self-delimiting pair encoding $\langle z_{[:i]}, z_{[i:]}\rangle$ when $|z| = 2i+1$, and the empty word when $|z|$ is even), $\pi_1, \pi_2$ for the two components of a pair encoding (the empty word when parsing fails), $Y = \pi_1(s(z))$ and $W = \pi_2(s(z))$; the code, input, width and clock fields of $z$ are $\pi_1(Y)$, $\pi_1(\pi_2(Y))$, $\pi_1(\pi_2(\pi_2(Y)))$ and $\pi_2(\pi_2(\pi_2(Y)))$. The guard $G(z)$ holds when $s(z)$, $Y$, $\pi_2(Y)$ and $\pi_2(\pi_2(Y))$ all parse as pair encodings and the width and clock fields consist only of ones, and the result for $z$ is $A_c(\alpha, \langle x, W_{[:n]}\rangle, t)$ when $G(z)$ holds, with $\alpha$, $x$ the code and input fields, $n$, $t$ the lengths of the width and clock fields and $W_{[:n]}$ the first $n$ bits of $W$, and $A_c(\varepsilon,\varepsilon,0)$ otherwise; here $A_c(\beta, v, t')$ is $1w'$ if $M_\beta$ run on $v$ for $t'$ steps has halted with output $w'$, and the single bit $0$ if it has not halted. Then for every bit string $z$, the result for $z$ equals $11$ if and only if $z \in V_c$, where $V_c$ is the set of strings $y'w'$ with $|w'| = |y'| + 1$ for which there are bit strings $\beta, v$ and $n', t' \in \mathbb{N}$ with $y' = \langle\beta,\langle v,\langle 1^{n'},1^{t'}\rangle\rangle\rangle$ such that $M_\beta$ halts on $\langle v, w'_{[:n']}\rangle$ within $t'$ steps with output exactly $1$, $w'_{[:n']}$ being the first $n'$ bits of $w'$.
